text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Monday:
- The crisis in the Swiss Defence Ministry is continuing as its boss, Defence Minister Adolf Ogi, and the chief of staff have different views on how to run the army.

- Swiss Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger said in an interview with the 'SonntagsZeitung' that he was annoyed about the fact that former Justice Minister Elisabeth Kopp and her husband pay no taxes. Kopp receives a pension of more that 200,000 francs a year. The couple owns several mansions.
- Bankrupt financier Werner Rey, in jail in the Bahamas, submitted another application for release on bail.

- Some 60,000 people have lost their jobs in the construction sector in the last six years in Switzerland. Bernard Koechli, chairman of one of the largest Swiss construction companies, Zschokke Holding, said that consolidation has not yet ended. - One month after beginning service, the so-called PendulAir, a shuttle service between Zurich and Geneva operated by Swissair, has not yet met expectations.
